submission.natural_language_explanation: This is a retrospective attributive-modifier detector: it fires on the token that completes a modifier inside a noun phrase - most strongly superlative/degree words (' most' straight after ' the', ' best', '-est'/'biggest'/'largest'), then attributive adjectives and past participles sitting before the noun they qualify ('the terrible table', 'the broken window'), and weakly on prepositions/coordinators that link two nouns ('the N of N', 'N and N'). Its strength is set by the modifier token itself and not by the head noun that follows (activation is identical across five different head nouns), while head nouns, verbs, determiners and attributive noun compounds ('the music industry') stay at the neuron's floor.

rival_explanations: Narrower token reading: the pole is essentially a ' most'/' best' detector plus their -est/-iest morphological variants, and the plain-adjective firings are spillover from those few very frequent tokens.
Broader pre-modifier reading: every pre-nominal modifier counts, so attributive nouns in compounds ('the music industry', 'the stone wall') should fire as strongly as adjectives do.
Lookahead reading: the pole prepares the noun head that the modifier introduces, so its activation should track the probability of the upcoming noun rather than the modifier's own identity.

First published by the London printer and

1807, the aim of this simple dice and board game was to collect as
many counters as possible to emulate the stereotypical Jewish
banker pictured in the centre of the board with his money bags.
The Broadway composer and collector Stephen

Aermacchi was an Italian aircraft manufacturer. Formerly known as Aeronautica Macchi, the company was founded in 1912 by Giulio Macchi at Varese in north-western Lombardy as Nieuport-Macchi, to build Nieuport monoplanes under licence for the Italian military. With a factory located on the shores of Lake Varese, the firm originally manufactured a series of Nieuport designs, as well as seaplanes.

After World War II, the company began producing motorcycles as a way to fill the post-war need for cheap, efficient transportation.

The company later specialised in civil and military pilot training aircraft. In July 2003, Aermacchi was integrated into the Finmeccanica Group (now Leonardo) as Alenia Aermacchi, which increased its shareholding to 99%.

Military trainers

 

Since the beginning, the design and production of military trainers have been the core business of Alenia Aermacchi.

The products include: 
 SF-260, piston-engined or turboprop-powered screener/primary trainer
 MB-326, turbofan engined trainer and light attack aircraft
 M-311, basic turbofan trainer
 MB-339CD, advanced and lead-in fighter trainer
 M-346, advanced and lead-in fighter trainer of the new generation

Military collaboration
Alenia Aermacchi has cooperated in international military programs:

 AMX program:
Alenia Aermacchi takes part in the AMX program with Alenia Aeronautica and Embraer of Brazil with a total share of 24%. Alenia Aermacchi develops and manufactures the fuselage forward and rear sections and installs some avionic equipment in the aircraft. A Mid-Life Updating program is required by the Italian Air Force to upgrade the aircraft capabilities.

 Panavia Tornado program:
Alenia Aermacchi designs and produces wing pylons and wing tips, roots, trailing edges and flaps, which represents a 5% share in the overall program.

 Eurofighter program:
Alenia Aermacchi has a share of more than 4% in the Eurofighter program, for the design and development of wing pylons, twin missile and twin store carriers, ECM pods, carbon fiber structures and titanium engine cowlings.

 C-27J program:
After participating in the G-222 transport aircraft program, the company is involved in the new Military Transport Aircraft C-27J Spartan, for the production of outer wings.

Civil programs

Since the mid-1990s, Alenia Aermacchi has participated in programs for the supply of engine nacelles for civil aircraft. It produces cold parts for engine nacelles: inlets, fan cowls and EBU, the systems-to-engine interface. 
In 1999, the company established a joint venture (MHD) with Hurel-Dubois (presently Hurel-Hispano, of SNECMA group). It is a French company specializing in the development and manufacture of thrust reversers, to obtain the full responsibility for the development of nacelles installed on maximum 100-seat aircraft.

Le tas (heap en anglais) est un des deux segments de mémoire utilisés lors de l'allocation dynamique de mémoire durant l'exécution d'un programme informatique.

L'autre segment de mémoire utilisé lors de l'allocation dynamique de mémoire est la pile d'exécution (call stack).

Lors de l'exécution d'un programme, le tas est utilisé pour allouer dynamiquement de l'espace mémoire à la demande du programme, par opposition à l'allocation dynamique sur la pile qui se fait automatiquement lors d'un appel de sous-routine ou de fonction.

La plupart des programmes ayant des besoins en mémoire dépendant de l'usage qu'on en fait, il est nécessaire de pouvoir demander au système, à des moments arbitraires de l'exécution, l'allocation de nouvelles zones de mémoire, et de pouvoir subséquemment restituer au système ces zones (désallouer la mémoire). Dans ce cas, l'allocation et la libération de la mémoire sont sous la responsabilité du programmeur. Les fuites de mémoire, ainsi que d'autres erreurs fréquentes dans les programmes à gestion manuelle de la mémoire, ont leur source dans les erreurs d'allocation mémoire sur le tas.

Classiquement, les fonctions de la bibliothèque standard du C malloc et free, ainsi que les opérateurs du langage C++ new et delete permettent, respectivement, d'allouer et désallouer la mémoire sur le tas.

adversarial_test_results.detail: 'forest' is a single token and a plain head noun (no 'est' piece), a role the hypothesis names as floor; the probe tests that head nouns outside any modifier stay quiet.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The interest rate stayed flat for a year, so the borrowers paid nothing extra on the loan, and the bank sent no notice.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'interest' is a single-token head noun in the compound 'interest rate' and 'flat' is predicative, both outside the modifier classes the hypothesis fires on; the compound keeps the broader reading firing.

adversarial_test_results.detail: The noun 'interest' shifted to a verb role ('did not interest'), which the hypothesis explicitly names as floor; the word is a single token, so only the part-of-speech change is tested.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lab will test the water again before the crew arrives on Monday, and the results go to the county office.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'test' is a verb, a role the hypothesis explicitly names as floor; the 'county office' compound keeps the broader pre-modifier reading firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The guest waited in the hall while the porter fetched the keys from the office, and then they went up the stairs together.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'guest' is a single-token head noun, a role the hypothesis names as floor; it is a word-shape near-miss with no modifier function.

adversarial_test_results.detail: A plain adjective in predicative position, outside the hypothesis's explicitly attributive firing class; it tests the attributive restriction itself, with no claimed trigger token present.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They will best the crew twice a year.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Some of the visitors left the hall early, but most stayed until midnight and helped clear the chairs.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'most' as a standalone pronoun/determiner with no noun of its own, predicted floor by the hypothesis and a fire by a ' most' token detector.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The forest floor was damp, and the ferns had begun to spread across the clearing near the gate.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'forest' is a single-token attributive noun inside the compound 'forest floor' and 'damp' is predicative; the hypothesis names compounds as floor, while the broader reading fires on the compound.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The crew loaded the cargo before dawn. The captain checked the manifest twice and counted the barrels. adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context hard negative built from compounds, head nouns and predicative adjectives only, all roles the hypothesis names as floor; it contains no ' most'/' best' token and no -est/-iest variant word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After the storm, the most remarkable rainbow appeared above the harbour, and the fishermen stopped to watch it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'the most' plus an attributive adjective in a topic unlike the examples; the hypothesis predicts a strong fire on the degree word and the adjective.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was the finest silverwork the auctioneer had handled in years, and he said so to everyone in the room.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Superlative -est adjective ('finest') outside the claimed token list, testing the hypothesis's -est generalization.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After comparing every quote twice, the committee chose the least expensive option on the list and signed the contract that afternoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Degree word 'least' plus an attributive adjective, a superlative-family paraphrase absent from the examples; tests the degree tier against a form-specific reader.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The neglected garden behind the chapel had grown wild, and the new caretaker promised to clear it before spring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Attributive past participle before its noun, the hypothesis's second tier, in a fresh context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lawyer read the delicious contract twice before signing, though he could not explain why it smelled of cinnamon.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was most unusual for the lake to freeze before December, a neighbour told the children.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The handle of the door had come loose again, so the carpenter brought a hinge and a screwdriver.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's weak tier: 'of' linking two nouns, with no superlative or attributive adjective anywhere in the probe.

adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's weak coordinator tier ('N and N'), with ' and' between two nouns; the 'kitchen table' compound keeps the broader pre-modifier and lookahead readings firing too.
